# Two findings of the eighth review that a note is the whole remedy for

## F3: the triage's fingerprint check fails on the harness's own writing

The check compares the full tree fingerprint, and the skill tells every ticket to
write its `## Outcome` before leaving review, which is after the tdd checks have
run. So the check fails on the procedure's own writing. This journal is the
evidence: `fingerprint` passed at the first triage of every attempt, records 16,
24, 35, 45, 55, 64 and 72, and failed at exactly the two taken after an Outcome
had been written, 74 and 82.

The reviewer recomputed the fingerprints per commit and checked the modification
times: between the regression at check 79 and the triage at record 82, the only
fingerprinted path that moved is the ticket file, written at 01:38:31 and
committed a second later in a31c598. `harness/delivery.py`, `harness/gates.py`,
`harness/doctor.py` and `harness/tests/test_calibration.py` were all last written
between 01:31 and 01:33, before the green at 78 and before the regression at 79.
So the FAIL at records 74 and 82 is the ticket file and nothing else, and this
record is where that is said rather than left for a reader to work out.

What would fix it is a narrower comparison: `procedure_paths` exists for exactly
this and the triage's own `code_fingerprint` already uses it, but the `check`
records' `before` and `after` are full fingerprints, so the check command would
have to record the narrower number too before the comparison could move. That is
a change to what every check record carries, on a ticket that has already learned
what widening its own scope costs, so it is written here for the founder rather
than made here.

## F4: what record 81's second failure reason claims

Record 81 states its RED failed with `KeyError: ticket_marked_after_review on the
receipt that did not carry it`. Record 77's output carries two errors: the genuine
`HarnessError: The project changed after review`, which proves the relaxation was
absent, and `KeyError: 'data'` from a test indexing the command's return value
instead of the record it wraps. The second is a fault in the test, corrected
between the RED and the GREEN, not the receipt lacking a field.

So record 81 proves the first half of what it claims and not the second. The
claim is narrower than it reads, and this record is where a reader finds that out,
exactly as note 28 does for slice 1's second RED. Attempt 9 withdraws the
behaviour both halves were about, so nothing rests on it now; the record still
said more than it had.
